## Why it fails with `ENOENT` (“no directory”)

`kobj->sd` is the kernfs sysfs directory node for a `device`/`kobject`. `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns` only warns/takes the `-ENOENT` path (line 1730-1732 vs. source returns -ENOENT) when **`parent == NULL`**. Since `dev` is non-NULL here (the `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` for-loop), `parent` is NULL because **`dev->kobj.sd` is NULL** — i.e., the USB device currently referenced by `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` has no kernfs directory. That happens on the boot-time UCSI event when the connector-change fires before the USB device has completed kernfs registration (`device_add`/`kobject_add` → `kobj->sd` set), or a stale `port->usb*_dev` points at an already torn-down device (`kobject_del` clears `sd`). The UCSI code then removes a `"typec"` link out of a directory that does not exist. The kernfs layer degrades this to `-ENOENT`, but the caller ignores the return, so it surfaces only as the `WARNING`. Note the stack line in your report (`dir.c:1706`) is the OEM build's shifted line number for the same NULL-parent warning.
